data.question: Do pinned official Lean and Nanoda reject the three prescribed symbolic-universe boundary violations while accepting each unchanged valid control?
data.versions: Lean 4.34.1 ARM64; Nanoda 3a240721; raw parser 076e8e5; exact binary/library/source hashes retained in protocol.json.
data.commands: run_process.py matrix 300 python3 run_matrix.py; six cases x (lean --run Replay.lean INPUT; nanoda_bin CONFIG). Exact argv and raw output retained per cell.
data.sample: Exactly three unchanged P1/M1/I1 controls and their three prescribed one-row invalid variants; two checkers, twelve initial cells. Six NDJSON files and all expectations bound in cases.json before observation.
data.controls: Acceptance requires explicit successful declaration completion. Official parser name/params/type/value output must exactly match cases.json, then explicit unknown-universe or declaration-type mismatch is checker rejection. Nanoda parser preserves raw parameters and level constructors by source inspection. Its all_uparams_defined assertion (tc.rs:554) and def_eq assertion (tc.rs:955) are expected checker-rejection panics; these are recorded separately from unrelated diagnostic crashes. A panic/exit alone does not establish rejection. Parser errors, unsupported results, timeouts and unclassified crashes remain separate incomplete observations. Any unexpected accept/reject needs source attribution; no automatic confirmation. Unchanged raw importer prints actual parsed forms before checking; missing parameter list and changed max expressions must survive. Nanoda consumes byte-identical files and source-bound raw constructors; rejected cases have no post-check pretty output. No runtime Nanoda AST trace or branch instrumentation is claimed.
